**Visa partners with OpenAI to enable payments by AI agents**

*Visa's deal to let AI agents transact across OpenAI's platform is the clearest signal yet that agentic commerce is moving from concept to infrastructure.*

Visa has formed a partnership with OpenAI that will allow AI agents operating on OpenAI's platform to initiate and complete payments using Visa's network. The arrangement positions Visa's rails as a default payment layer for autonomous software agents, a category that both card networks and tech platforms have begun treating as a near-term commercial reality rather than a research curiosity.

The partnership follows a pattern of network-level moves to capture agentic payment flows before they crystallise around alternative rails. Mastercard has made similar signals, and Santander's Getnet launched agent-initiated merchant acceptance earlier this month. What distinguishes the Visa-OpenAI tie-up is the scale of OpenAI's consumer and enterprise user base, which gives the integration immediate distribution.

For European payments professionals, the development sharpens a question that PSD3 and the Payment Services Regulation will need to answer: how agent-initiated transactions fit within existing consent, authentication and liability frameworks. If AI agents become a meaningful payment initiation channel, the regulatory treatment of delegated authority and strong customer authentication will require specificity that current drafts do not yet provide.

*Sources: [Visa and OpenAI form agentic commerce partnership](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/47900/visa-and-openai-form-agentic-commerce-partnership) — Finextra*

**ECB launches cross-currency instant payments between euro area, Denmark and Sweden**

*TIPS now settles instant payments across euros, Danish kroner and Swedish kronor, creating the first live cross-currency instant payment link in Europe.*

The European Central Bank has activated cross-currency settlement on its TIPS infrastructure, enabling payment service providers to send instant payments between accounts denominated in euros, Danish kroner and Swedish kronor. The service went live on June 10, marking the first time TIPS has operated across multiple currencies.

This is a practical milestone for the ECB's ambition to make TIPS a pan-European utility rather than a eurozone-only system. Denmark and Sweden, both EU members outside the euro area, have been working towards TIPS integration for several years. The go-live means a euro-denominated payment can now reach a recipient's Swedish krona account in seconds, with currency conversion handled within the settlement process.

The immediate user base is limited to PSPs connected to TIPS in those three currencies, but the architecture is designed to accommodate additional currencies. Norway, which is not an EU member but has explored TIPS participation, is one obvious candidate. For banks and payment processors operating across the Nordics and the eurozone, this reduces the case for maintaining separate domestic and cross-border instant payment channels.

*Sources: [Cross-currency payments between the euro area, Denmark and Sweden](https://www.ecb.europa.eu/press/intro/news/html/ecb.mipnews260610.en.html) — European Central Bank | [Cross-currency payments between the euro area, Denmark and Sweden go live](https://www.finextra.com/pressarticle/110099/cross-currency-payments-between-the-euro-area-denmark-and-sweden-go-live) — Finextra*

**Euro Banking Association maps agentic AI's role in open finance**

*A new EBA report argues that AI agents acting autonomously within open finance frameworks could reshape embedded finance, but flags unresolved questions on liability and consent.*

The Euro Banking Association's Open Finance Working Group has published a report examining how agentic AI could accelerate embedded finance within open finance ecosystems. The report, titled "Supercharging Embedded Finance", explores scenarios in which AI agents autonomously access financial data and initiate transactions on behalf of consumers and businesses using open finance APIs.

The working group identifies agentic AI as a potential amplifier for open finance adoption, arguing that autonomous agents could drive usage of data-sharing and payment initiation services at a scale and frequency that exceeds manual consumer interaction. The report describes use cases such as agents that continuously optimise treasury positions, auto-switch financial products, or trigger payments based on real-time conditions.

The report also flags governance gaps. Current open finance frameworks assume a human in the loop for consent and authentication. AI agents acting with delegated authority complicate that model, raising questions about liability allocation when an agent acts on stale consent or makes a suboptimal decision. The timing is notable: this is the second publication in a week, after the Visa-OpenAI announcement, to force the question of where autonomous agents sit within European payments regulation.

*Sources: [EBA Report Says Agentic AI Is Poised to Supercharge Embedded Finance](https://financialit.net/news/artificial-intelligence/eba-report-says-agentic-ai-poised-supercharge-embedded-finance) — Financial IT*

**BoursoBank integrates Wero for person-to-person payments in France**

*France's largest online bank has added Wero to its payment offering, extending the European payment scheme's reach beyond its initial German footprint.*

BoursoBank, France's largest online bank with over seven million customers, has integrated Wero into its payment services. The integration enables BoursoBank customers to send and receive person-to-person instant payments through Wero, which operates on the SEPA instant credit transfer rail.

The move is significant for Wero's geographic expansion. The scheme, backed by the European Payments Initiative, launched first in Germany and Belgium. ING's rollout to 10 million German customers was covered last week. BoursoBank's adoption brings a major French institution onto the platform and tests whether Wero can gain traction in a market where Paylib, the incumbent French mobile payment scheme, already has substantial user penetration.

BoursoBank is owned by Société Générale, one of EPI's founding shareholders. The integration is therefore expected rather than surprising, but it matters for Wero's credibility as a pan-European scheme. Each major-market launch that reaches millions of end users strengthens the network effects that Wero needs to compete with established card-based and wallet-based alternatives.

*Sources: [BoursoBank Integrates Wero Into Its Payment Solutions](https://ffnews.com/newsarticle/paytech/boursobank-integrates-wero-into-its-payment-solutions/) — FF News*

**Token.io appoints Mondu's Gil Danziger as chief technology officer**

*The open banking infrastructure provider has hired Gil Danziger from buy-now-pay-later firm Mondu as its new CTO.*

Token.io has appointed Gil Danziger as its new chief technology officer. Danziger joins from Mondu, a B2B buy-now-pay-later provider, where he held a senior technology role. Token.io provides open banking payment infrastructure used by banks, payment service providers and merchants to initiate payments directly from customer bank accounts.

The source does not indicate whether this is a newly created role or a replacement. Token.io has been expanding its account-to-account payment capabilities across European markets and recently extended its coverage to additional banking APIs. A CTO appointment at this stage likely reflects the operational demands of scaling infrastructure across fragmented European bank connectivity, though the company has not stated a specific strategic rationale.

*Sources: [Token.io appoints Gil Danziger as new CTO](https://www.fintechfutures.com/job-cuts-new-hires/token-io-appoints-gil-danziger-as-new-cto) — FinTech Futures*
